What are your favorites and least favorite songs off each album?

Good question, I'll be using the UK releases for this one!

Please Please Me: I love 'There's a Place' and I'm not a fan of 'Boys' because I'm not all the sold on Ringo's voice here.

With The Beatles: 'You Really Got a Hold on Me' is my favourite, it's a Smokey Robinson cover and it just sits with me nicely, love John's singing. Dislike 'I Wanna Be Your Man', sorry Ringo!

A Hard Day's Night: I love 'Things We Said Today' because as a guitar player I love how McCartney goes between A and Am (A minor) and makes it sound perfectly natural. 'I'm Happy Just To Dance With You' is a turn off for me, not sure why it just doesn't do it for me.

Beatles For Sale: 'Eight Days a Week' is great, 'What You're Doing' is weak and not a big one with me.

Help!: 'Ticket To Ride' is an ace track but I'm not a fan of 'Another Girl'.

Rubber Soul: This is a hard one to choose from but I love 'In My Life' and have little time for 'Run For Your Life'.

Revolver: 'Tomorrow Never Knows', ground-breaking back then and still other-worldy in 2015. There's 2 tracks I'm not that big on but I'll go with 'Yellow Submarine' Sorry again Ringo!

Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band: No question 'A Day in the Life', probably my favourite Beatles song ever. Least liked on this one is probably 'Fixing a Hole'. It's a perfectly good song and good lyrics but it just never hit it off with me.

Magical Mystery Tour: Unquestionably 'Strawberry Fields Forever', the let down for me is 'Your Mother Should Know'.

The Beatles (The White Album): This is the hardest out of all of them but I guess it would be 'While My Guitar Gently Weeps' for my best song and the worst for me is 'Ob-La-Di, Ob-La-Da'.

Yellow Submarine: 'Hey Bulldog' should've been a A-side single release, great song. 'It's All Too Much' for me is the worst more for the muddy production than the actual song.

Abbey Road: Can I cheat here? The entire side 2 medley is the best. The worst song for me is 'Maxwell's Silver Hammer'.

Let It Be: I really like 'Two Of Us' and I'll pass on Maggie Mae.
